title: block-drive input spec
description:
Inputs to one ``block-drive`` tick.

Both fields are optional so a bare tick can recover its position purely from
durable state: on a RESUME the ``run_id`` names the parked run whose
``pending_decision`` + decision journal carry everything; on a FRESH start the
``workflow`` names which chain (``submit`` / ``status`` / ``aggregate`` /
``campaign``) to begin. ``dry_run`` prints the planned action without
executing any span.

run_id.description: The run being driven. On a RESUME this keys the pending_decision + decision-journal reads that recover the parked position; on a FRESH start it is the run the first span will operate on.
run_id.title: Run Id

workflow.description: The workflow family to drive (submit / status / aggregate / campaign). Required for a FRESH chain start (picks the first block from block_chain.ORDER); recovered from the resume cursor on a RESUME.
workflow.title: Workflow

audit.description: The AUDIT chain's non-run scope seat (P2.b) — required to FRESH-start `workflow: "audit"`, ignored by every other family. A notebook audit is keyed by audit_id and mints no run, so `run_id` cannot start it.

dry_run.description: Print the planned action and exit without executing any span.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

approve.description: FUSED commit+advance (L1). An append-decision payload (the SAME AppendDecisionInput shape: scope_kind / scope_id / block / response / resolved / etc). When set, this ONE call first commits the human's y/nudge through the single append_decision definition — every authorship / brief-provenance / code-derived-field / bare-ack / unlock-authorship gate fires IDENTICALLY to a standalone `append-decision` — then advances the driver in the same call, returning the next parked brief. It removes the agent's mechanical SECOND call (the old `append-decision` then `block-drive` pair becomes one). MECHANISM only: the human still utters the y.
approve.title: Approve

BlockDriveAuditSeat.description:
The AUDIT chain's scope declaration (P2.b) — a NON-run scope.

A notebook audit is keyed by ``audit_id`` and mints no run, so the driver's
``run_id``-based fresh-entry materialization cannot start it. This is the
seat the caller declares instead: the audit scope plus the two ``.py`` paths
every block in the chain is composed from. The driver hands it VERBATIM to
``audit-preflight`` (whose spec model is what validates it), and every
downstream block's spec is code-composed from what the predecessor emits —
the agent never re-authors a spec mid-chain.

audit_id.description: The notebook decision-journal scope the whole chain is keyed by.
audit_id.title: Audit Id

source.description: Experiment-relative path to the audited source .py. Its PRESENCE is the chain's draft-readiness test: absent, the first tick parks for the agent to draft it rather than chaining into a lint of nothing.
source.title: Source

template.description: Experiment-relative path to the template .py (the required inventory).
template.title: Template

source_roots.description: Optional OPAQUE import roots for the preflight's roots check. Null defaults them from the audit's recorded configuration (the one-declaration rule).
source_roots.title: Source Roots

input_roots.description: Optional OPAQUE data-path roots for the preflight's roots check. Null defaults them from the audit's recorded configuration.
input_roots.title: Input Roots

BlockDriveAuditSeat.title: block-drive audit seat
